newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-BOLDEN READY TO WIN AT WORLD INDOORS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BOLDEN READY TO WIN AT WORLD INDOORS.

text.p: Buoyed by running the world's fourth fastest time ever in the 200 meters indoors this season, Ato Bolden says he is ready to win at this weekend's World Indoor Track Championships in Paris.
"It's time for gold," Bolden said in a tele-conference call from Atlanta at the weekly New York Track Writers Luncheon before leaving Monday night for Paris.
"I feel that if I go there and run what I am suppose to run, I'll be ok," said Bolden, who was a bronze medalist in both the 100 meters and 200 meters in last year's Olympics.
Bolden left for Paris still considering running in the 60-meter sprint but leaning toward the 200 meters. He said he would run at only one distance because of the schedule.
Bolden ran a sizzling 20.35 seconds in his first 200 meters this season to win at Birmingham, England, last month. It appears likely he will choose the 200 meters in Paris.
"The fact that I have opened up the way I did is very exciting because it tells me that I'm on the right track," Bolden, 23, said.
The circumstances are in Bolden's advantage this week to win because superstar Michael Johnson will not be in the field. Johnson has not raced at all this indoor season.

"You would like to have the absolute best, the world record holder in your race, and beat him," Bolden said of the American, who set the record of 19.30 seconds in last year's Atlanta Games where he became the first man to win gold medals in both the 200 and 400 meters.
But if Bolden wins, he does not think his victory will be tainted because Johnson did not compete.
"It is just that they will record it as me being the world champion, and I have to look at it like that," Bolden said.
Bolden knows how his fans back home in Trinidad will look at his win.
"Believe me Trinidad & Tobago wll be very happy with the gold, regardless of who was there," Bolden said. "They will really enjoy this and this is really a run for them."
